column1: # What each fixture's output shows, as (label, value, stream) facts.
# Read by cli/tests/reporting_facts.rs, which runs every fixture below in a
# fresh copy of this directory and fails on any fact it cannot find. A change
# to what camdl shows is therefore an edit to this file, made in the same
# commit as the change, with the reason in the commit message. Hashes,
# timings and absolute paths are not facts and are not recorded.
#   run     the command that shows the fact (the list is in the test file)
#   stream  stdout or stderr; or events, the events.jsonl of the leaf the
#           run wrote (one JSON object per line, docs/camdl-run-spec.md §10.11)
#   scope   line: the value is on a line that contains the label
#           block: the value is on a line containing the label, or on a later
#                  line before the next blank line (the label heads a section)
#   label   text that names the fact
# A label may match several lines; the fact holds if any of them carries the
# value. The fixtures are deliberately small runs, not the tutorial's fits:
# pmmh_stuck leaves two of four chains at the proposal-scale floor, fail has
# every chain refused at its start, pfilter.toml is a fit whose method is a
# particle filter at fixed parameters. cases.tsv is
# Fixed seeds make the draws reproducible on one platform, not bit-identical
# across libm implementations. Bulk and classic R-hat are stable to the printed
# digits under last-bit differences in the draws; folded R-hat is not, because
# |x - median| puts near-ties around the median whose ranks flip (PGAS gamma's
# folded R-hat is 1.263 on macOS and 1.271 on Linux CI). PGAS folded values
# are therefore not recorded; PMMH's matched on both platforms.
